record.notes: The current NIST pages use CAISSI. The name-history start is the earliest archived use of the name found, NIST's super intelligence page as captured on 30 September 2026. Executive Order 14434 of 29 September 2026, which directs the executive branch to use 'Super Intelligence' in place of 'Artificial Intelligence', is the likely trigger, but it does not name this centre or set a date for its rename. The current ministerial basis refers to the June 2025 CAISI decision; the retained establishment date refers to its US AISI predecessor. Canada's CAISI, the Canadian AI Safety Institute, is a different body.

testing_capacity.notes: The institute was renamed from CAISI to CAISSI after Executive Order 14434 (29 September 2026), which does not name it; the GLM-5.3 assessment predates the rename. Evaluators from across government take part through the TRAINS Taskforce, which the institute convenes, so this is not testing by other bodies.

model_access.notes: Event dates are the model's public release date in Epoch AI's data unless the source dates the access itself; the sources state that the access came before release, so the access took place on or before that date. The Epoch AI models cited for the leading-developer test were released at least a month before each such date. NIST's release of 5 May 2026 says 'developers frequently provide CAISI with models that have reduced or removed safeguards' and that the institute 'has completed more than 40 such evaluations, including on state-of-the-art models that remain unreleased'; it names no model or developer for this access, so it is not a dated event. Not counted: GLM-5.3 (Z.ai, September 2026) and Kimi K3 (Moonshot, July 2026), assessed after public release with no access route stated; the June 2024 Claude 3.5 Sonnet testing, which the UK institute ran and 'shared their results with the US AI Safety Institute'; the Llama 3.1-405B network pilot, whose weights are public; and Claude Opus 5.5 (September 2026), whose system card says Anthropic 'collaborated with the U.S. Center for AI Standards and Innovation (CAISI)' on measurement without stating pre-release access. Microsoft has had no model in Epoch AI's frontier set released since 1 January 2023; its latest there is Megatron-Turing NLG 530B (2021, with Nvidia). No legal power: Executive Order 14434 has no access provision for the institute.

claims.text: The Commerce Department's statement says it will lead unclassified evaluations of AI capabilities that may pose risks to national security.
NIST's report says it evaluated the open-weight model DeepSeek V4 Pro in April 2026.
The Commerce Department's statement says it will coordinate with other federal agencies to develop evaluation methods.
NIST says it requested public comment on a draft document, NIST AI 800-2 Practices for Automated Benchmark Evaluations of Language Models.
NIST's announcement says it held three practitioner workshops and conducted a literature review on the challenges of post-deployment monitoring of AI systems.
NIST's announcement says it and the UK AI Security Institute ran a joint evaluation of Moonshot AI's Kimi K3.
The Commerce Department's statement says it will serve as industry's primary point of contact in the US government to facilitate testing and collaborative research on commercial AI systems.
NIST's announcement says the TRAINS Taskforce is chaired by it and includes representation from federal agencies.
Its introduction in a NIST AI update lists supporting the diffusion and adoption of AI throughout the US economy.
NIST's post describes the then CAISI as one way NIST supports the American AI industry through collaborative research on AI metrology and model evaluations.
